properties.trigger: any competition tagged american_football, from flag and school leagues to the national pro league: games, box scores, rosters, depth charts, standings, playoffs, the draft, free agency, trades, byes
properties.scope: competition, season, team, person, event, stat_line

data.short_description: American football at every level, with the national 32-team pro league as the reference: positions, stages and weeks, the full box-score stat key set, standings columns and tiebreaker order, roster and reserve-list rules, officials, and how real players are shared with fantasy.

lore.title: Overview
lore.content:
Sport: American football. Code american_football. A match is a game. Four quarters (15 minutes at the professional and college levels, 12 in school leagues, 8-10 or two running-clock halves in rec and flag leagues), halftime after the second. The single score number is points: touchdown 6, extra point 1, two-point conversion 2, field goal 3, safety 2 (flag leagues vary; see Recreational). event.periods stays empty in this sport: quarter scores live on each team's match stat_line as points_q1..points_ot (Stat keys, continued). Overtime rules depend on the level and are in the Professional and Recreational chunks; a game still level when the league's overtime is exhausted is a tie.
Results: home_win, away_win, tie. Never draw. no_result only for a cancelled game that is neither rescheduled nor forfeited. decided_by: regulation, overtime, run_rule (a rec or school game stopped early at a margin), called_game (a game the league counts as final from the point it was stopped).
score_display carries what the numbers lose: "27-24 OT", "20-20 OT tie", "2-0 (forfeit)", "35-7 (mercy, 3rd qtr)".
Default competition values: level pro, college, youth or recreational as fits; format league_playoffs; scoring_system win_loss. Seasons are labelled by the year the regular season starts (a pro season that starts in September 2026 and ends with a championship game in February 2027 is "2026"). Season tag is <competition-fragment>-<label>, e.g. proleague-2026, flag-fall-2026.
Every entity in this sport carries the tag american_football. The pack governs any competition in the sport: the national 32-team professional league, a college conference, a school district league, a Thursday flag league. A generic league shape for the 32-team, two-conference, eight-division shape ships as league-shapes/pro-league-32-two-conferences.json; onboarding renames its placeholder teams and, when it creates the first season, writes each team's COMPETES_IN conference and group from the team's conference-* and division-* tags.
Home and away: the designated home team is home even at a neutral or overseas stadium (a pro game played abroad, a school game at a county field); HELD_AT points at the actual venue and neutral_site stays false unless the league designates neither side as home (the championship game, a bowl game, a rec tournament final), in which case neutral_site true with neutral_first for the team the league lists first.
Byes: not a game. Record a bye as an event with event_type bye, status completed, stage regular_season, round "Week N", name "<Team> — Bye — Week N", PART_OF the season, INVOLVED_IN from the team with role subject, tag bye. Byes never touch standings: this pack awards no bye points.

lore.title: Positions
lore.content:
Position codes for PLAYS_FOR position and secondary_positions. Use the most specific code the owner gives; fall back to the group code.
Offense:
QB  quarterback
RB  running back (halfback)
FB  fullback
WR  wide receiver
TE  tight end
LT  left tackle
LG  left guard
C   center
RG  right guard
RT  right tackle
OT  offensive tackle (side unknown)
OG  offensive guard (side unknown)
OL  offensive lineman (generic)
Defense:
DE  defensive end
DT  defensive tackle
NT  nose tackle
EDGE edge rusher (4-3 DE or 3-4 OLB when the owner uses the modern label)
OLB outside linebacker
ILB inside linebacker
MLB middle linebacker
LB  linebacker (generic)
CB  cornerback
NB  nickel back / slot corner
FS  free safety
SS  strong safety
S   safety (generic)
DB  defensive back (generic)
Special teams:
K   placekicker
P   punter
LS  long snapper
KR  kick returner (secondary position only)
PR  punt returner (secondary position only)
Flag leagues: QB, WR, RB (if rushing exists), C, and on defense DB, LB, EDGE (the rusher); map the owner's words to the closest code.
Depth chart: the order at a position is depth_order on PLAYS_FOR (1 = QB1, 2 = QB2, 3 = QB3); role is starter for depth_order 1 at the eleven offensive and eleven defensive spots plus K, P and LS, bench for the rest of the active roster, practice_squad for the practice squad, injured_reserve for players on the injured list and reserve for players on any other reserve list; roster_list names the list itself (Roster rules). A player who starts at two positions keeps one PLAYS_FOR edge with position and secondary_positions. Record "QB1" or "WR3" as position QB + depth_order 1, position WR + depth_order 3, never as a position code. Depth charts change weekly; update depth_order in place and let PLAYED_IN started say who actually started a given game.

lore.title: Stages and rounds
lore.content:
stage values for events and the season's stage property:
offseason      between the final and the next camp (season.stage only; events in it are drafts, signings, trades, tryouts)
preseason      exhibition or scrimmage games; round "Preseason Week N" or "Scrimmage"
regular_season round "Week N" (always "Week 9", never "Wk 9" or "W9", so filters match)
wildcard       first playoff round in a league that has one; round "Wild Card"
divisional     second playoff round in the pro format; round "Divisional"
quarterfinal   rec, college and school brackets of 8; round "Quarterfinal"
semifinal      round "Semifinal" (the pro format uses conference instead)
conference     conference championship games; round "Conference A Championship" as the league names it
final          the championship game: the pro league's title game, a state final, a bowl game, a rec title game; round names it as the league does ("Championship Game 61", "State Final", "Fall Championship")
consolation    third-place or consolation-bracket games
all_star       all-star exhibitions at any level; never counted
Season.current_round is the same "Week N" string. Season.rounds_total is the number of weeks including byes (18 in the pro format), not the number of games (17).
decided_by: regulation, overtime, run_rule (rec and school leagues that stop a lopsided game early; the result stands), called_game (an abandoned game the league counts as final at the stoppage; see Forfeits and abandonments). Nothing else exists in this sport; forfeits are status forfeited with the league's awarded score and a lore note that is never a medical reason.
Event naming: "<Away> at <Home> — <YYYY-MM-DD>" with full team names, e.g. "Riverside Rovers at Harbor City Hawks — 2026-11-08". Kickoff time in date_hour/date_minute in the stadium's local time, timezone when the world spans zones. If the owner only gives a broadcast window ("1:00 ET"), store that hour with timezone America/New_York.

lore.title: Stat keys
lore.content:
All keys lowercase snake_case, values numbers (sacks may be x.5; everything else integers unless marked). null = not recorded. Rate stats marked DERIVED are never stored; the AI computes them from the components when asked and says so. Fantasy keys (fantasy_points, projected_points) are stored on lines RECORDED_IN the fantasy matchup (see the Fantasy chunk and the base rule/app_fantasy), never the real game.

PLAYER — general
games_started            games in the starting lineup (season/career lines; match lines use PLAYED_IN started)
snaps_offense            offensive snaps played
snaps_defense            defensive snaps played
snaps_special_teams      special-teams snaps played

PLAYER — passing
pass_attempts            passes thrown (sacks are not attempts)
pass_completions         passes completed
passing_yards            passing yards (sack yards are NOT subtracted for a player)
passing_touchdowns       touchdown passes
interceptions_thrown     passes intercepted
sacks_taken              times sacked
sack_yards_lost          yards lost on sacks
longest_pass             longest completion, yards
passing_first_downs      completions that gained a first down
passes_20_plus           completions of 20+ yards
completion_pct           DERIVED = pass_completions / pass_attempts * 100
yards_per_attempt        DERIVED = passing_yards / pass_attempts
passer_rating            DERIVED, the standard pro formula: a = clamp((pass_completions/pass_attempts - 0.3) * 5), b = clamp((passing_yards/pass_attempts - 3) * 0.25), c = clamp(passing_touchdowns/pass_attempts * 20), d = clamp(2.375 - interceptions_thrown/pass_attempts * 25); each clamped to 0..2.375; rating = (a+b+c+d) / 6 * 100
touchdown_pct            DERIVED = passing_touchdowns / pass_attempts * 100
interception_pct         DERIVED = interceptions_thrown / pass_attempts * 100

PLAYER — rushing
rush_attempts            carries
rushing_yards            rushing yards (net, kneel-downs included as the league counts them)
rushing_touchdowns       rushing touchdowns
longest_rush             longest carry, yards
rushing_first_downs      carries that gained a first down
rushes_20_plus           carries of 20+ yards
yards_per_carry          DERIVED = rushing_yards / rush_attempts

PLAYER — receiving
targets                  passes thrown to the player
receptions               catches
receiving_yards          receiving yards
receiving_touchdowns     receiving touchdowns
longest_reception        longest catch, yards
receiving_first_downs    catches that gained a first down
yards_after_catch        yards gained after the catch
drops                    catchable passes dropped (owner's or source's judgement)
yards_per_reception      DERIVED = receiving_yards / receptions
yards_per_target         DERIVED = receiving_yards / targets
catch_pct                DERIVED = receptions / targets * 100

PLAYER — ball security and scoring
fumbles                  fumbles by the player
fumbles_lost             fumbles recovered by the opponent
fumbles_recovered_own    own or teammates' fumbles the player recovered
two_point_conversions    successful two-point conversions the player scored (pass, rush or catch)
scrimmage_yards          DERIVED = rushing_yards + receiving_yards
all_purpose_yards        DERIVED = rushing_yards + receiving_yards + kick_return_yards + punt_return_yards + interception_return_yards + fumble_return_yards
total_touchdowns         DERIVED = rushing_touchdowns + receiving_touchdowns + kick_return_touchdowns + punt_return_touchdowns + interception_touchdowns + fumble_touchdowns (passing touchdowns are NOT the passer's)

PLAYER — defense
tackles_solo             solo tackles
tackles_assisted         assisted tackles
tackles_total            DERIVED = tackles_solo + tackles_assisted
tackles_for_loss         tackles behind the line of scrimmage (sacks included as the league counts them)
sacks                    sacks; half-sacks as 0.5 (flag: flag pulls behind the line)
qb_hits                  quarterback hits
interceptions            passes intercepted by the player
interception_return_yards  yards returned on interceptions
interception_touchdowns  interceptions returned for a touchdown
passes_defended          passes broken up or intercepted
forced_fumbles           fumbles forced
fumble_recoveries        opponent fumbles recovered
fumble_return_yards      yards returned on fumble recoveries
fumble_touchdowns        fumbles returned for a touchdown
safeties                 safeties scored by the player
blocked_kicks            field goals, punts or extra points blocked
defensive_touchdowns     DERIVED = interception_touchdowns + fumble_touchdowns

PLAYER — kicking
field_goals_made         field goals made
field_goals_attempted    field goals attempted (blocked kicks count as attempts)
fg_made_under_40         made from 39 yards or less
fg_attempted_under_40    attempted from 39 yards or less
fg_made_40_49            made from 40-49
fg_attempted_40_49       attempted from 40-49
fg_made_50_plus          made from 50+
fg_attempted_50_plus     attempted from 50+
longest_field_goal       longest made, yards
extra_points_made        extra points made
extra_points_attempted   extra points attempted
kickoffs                 kickoffs
touchbacks               kickoffs resulting in a touchback
field_goal_pct           DERIVED = field_goals_made / field_goals_attempted * 100
kicking_points           DERIVED = field_goals_made * 3 + extra_points_made

PLAYER — punting
punts                    punts
punt_yards               gross punt yards
longest_punt             longest punt, yards
punts_inside_20          punts downed inside the 20
punt_touchbacks          punts that went for a touchback
punts_blocked            punts blocked
punt_return_yards_allowed  return yards on the player's punts (needed for net)
punt_gross_average       DERIVED = punt_yards / punts
punt_net_average         DERIVED = (punt_yards - punt_return_yards_allowed - 20 * punt_touchbacks) / punts

PLAYER — returns
kick_returns             kickoff returns
kick_return_yards        kickoff return yards
kick_return_touchdowns   kickoffs returned for a touchdown
longest_kick_return      longest kickoff return, yards
punt_returns             punt returns
punt_return_yards        punt return yards
punt_return_touchdowns   punts returned for a touchdown
longest_punt_return      longest punt return, yards
kick_return_average      DERIVED = kick_return_yards / kick_returns
punt_return_average      DERIVED = punt_return_yards / punt_returns

PLAYER — discipline
penalties                penalties called on the player
penalty_yards            yards those penalties cost

lore.title: Stat keys (continued)
lore.content:
TEAM — match line (one stat_line per team per game, scope match, RECORDED_IN the game). The final score stays on the event; do not repeat it here.
points_q1, points_q2, points_q3, points_q4, points_ot   points by period (points_ot null when no overtime; halves-based leagues use points_q1 and points_q3 for the two halves and leave q2/q4 null, and say so in House rules)
first_downs              total first downs
first_downs_rushing      first downs by rush
first_downs_passing      first downs by pass
first_downs_penalty      first downs by penalty
total_plays              offensive plays (rushes + pass attempts + sacks taken)
total_yards              net yards of offense
rushing_attempts         team carries
rushing_yards            team rushing yards
pass_completions         team completions
pass_attempts            team pass attempts
net_passing_yards        passing yards minus sack yards lost (team passing is net)
sacks_allowed            times the team's passers were sacked
sack_yards_lost          yards lost to sacks
third_down_conversions   third downs converted
third_down_attempts      third downs faced
fourth_down_conversions  fourth downs converted
fourth_down_attempts     fourth downs attempted
red_zone_trips           drives reaching the opponent's 20
red_zone_touchdowns      red-zone drives ending in a touchdown
penalties                penalties against the team (accepted)
penalty_yards            penalty yards against the team
turnovers                giveaways = fumbles_lost + interceptions_thrown (stored, because sources report it directly)
fumbles_lost             fumbles lost
interceptions_thrown     passes intercepted by the opponent
takeaways                opponent turnovers forced
defensive_sacks          sacks by the team's defense
defensive_touchdowns     touchdowns scored by the defense (stored on the team line because sources report it; DERIVED on player lines)
return_touchdowns        kick and punt returns for a touchdown by the team
safeties                 safeties scored by the team's defense
blocked_kicks            kicks the team's defense blocked
time_of_possession_seconds  time of possession in seconds (32:14 = 1934); the AI formats mm:ss when presenting
punts                    team punts
field_goals_made, field_goals_attempted   team kicking
kick_return_yards, punt_return_yards      team return yards
explosive_plays          plays of 20+ yards (optional, when the source gives it)
yards_per_play           DERIVED = total_yards / total_plays
third_down_pct           DERIVED = third_down_conversions / third_down_attempts * 100
red_zone_pct             DERIVED = red_zone_touchdowns / red_zone_trips * 100
turnover_margin          DERIVED = takeaways - turnovers

TEAM — season line (the standings cache; scope season, RECORDED_IN the season; regular-season games only)
wins, losses, ties
points_for               points scored, regular season
points_against           points allowed, regular season
division_wins, division_losses, division_ties
conference_wins, conference_losses, conference_ties
home_wins, home_losses, home_ties
away_wins, away_losses, away_ties
point_differential       DERIVED = points_for - points_against
win_pct                  DERIVED = (wins + 0.5 * ties) / (wins + losses + ties)
strength_of_victory      DERIVED: combined win_pct of all opponents the team beat (a team beaten twice counts twice)
strength_of_schedule     DERIVED: combined win_pct of all opponents played
Season aggregates of every player and team match key above may also appear on a season line (passing_yards for a QB over the year, total_yards for a team), summed per rule/stats. Streaks ("W3") are not stored; derive them from COMPETED_IN edges when asked.

lore.title: Standings
lore.content:
Keys on a team season line: wins, losses, ties, points_for, points_against, division_wins/losses/ties, conference_wins/losses/ties, home_* and away_*. games_played = wins + losses + ties. Count only events with stage regular_season and status completed or forfeited; preseason, all_star and playoff games never enter the table.
Columns to show, per division or group, in this order: Team, W, L, T, PCT, PF, PA, Net Pts, Div, Conf, Home, Away, Streak (drop Div/Conf when the league has no divisions). Division membership for the season is on COMPETES_IN: conference holds the conference ("Conference A") and group holds the division alone ("East", "Blue Division", "Tuesday Co-ed"), each written as the league writes it; a league with no conferences leaves conference empty. In the two-conference pro shape that is two conference values and four group values. A division game is one where both teams' conference and group match; a conference game is one where only conference matches.
Order by win_pct, then the tiebreakers. The national pro league's order below is the sport's reference list; rec, school and college leagues usually use steps 1-4 and then points allowed or a coin toss, and say so in a House rules chunk on the competition. Apply the steps in order and restart from the top whenever a step reduces the tied group.
Division tiebreakers:
1. Head-to-head record among the tied teams (best combined record in games between them).
2. Division record.
3. Record in common games (games against the same opponents).
4. Conference record.
5. Strength of victory.
6. Strength of schedule.
7. Best combined ranking among conference teams in points scored and points allowed.
8. Best combined ranking among all teams in points scored and points allowed.
9. Net points in common games.
10. Net points in all games.
11. Net touchdowns in all games.
12. Coin toss (report "coin toss" and leave the order as the owner says).
Wild card and seeding (seeds 5-7, and ordering division winners 1-4): if two tied teams are from the same division, the division tiebreaker settles them first and only the survivor moves on. Then: 1. head-to-head, only if one team swept or was swept by every other tied team; 2. conference record; 3. common games, minimum four; 4. strength of victory; 5. strength of schedule; 6-11 as the division list from step 7 down. Division winners are seeded 1-4 by record then these tiebreakers; wild cards 5-7 likewise.
Always name the tiebreaker that split any tied teams and say how many games the lines cover. If the owner has not logged every game of the season (most fans log only their team), say the table is partial and give only what the record supports: usually their own team's record and division record, never a fabricated league table. Head-to-head, division and conference records are read straight from COMPETED_IN edges and the opponents' COMPETES_IN conference and group; strength of victory and schedule need every opponent's full record, so say when they cannot be computed.
Pro playoff shape: 7 seeds per conference; wildcard round pairs 2v7, 3v6, 4v5 with the higher seed at home; the 1 seed rests. Divisional: the 1 seed hosts the lowest surviving seed. Conference championship at the higher seed. Championship game neutral. Set COMPETES_IN seed when clinched, status eliminated when out, outcome playoffs for any team that made it, runner_up for the championship-game loser, champion for the winner; WON from the champion to the season with title "Champion" and detail the game's number and score.

lore.title: Roster rules
lore.content:
Eleven a side on the field (flag: 5, 7 or 8; see Recreational). Unlimited substitution between plays, so minutes are not tracked; snaps_* keys carry playing time when the owner has them. PLAYED_IN started means in the starting lineup on offense, defense or as K/P; played false means dressed or on the roster but did not take a snap (no reason recorded).
Roster size, game-day actives, practice squads and reserve lists are league rules and live in the Professional chunk or a House rules chunk on the competition. Before logging a lineup, check the competition's House rules chunk for squad size and any eligibility rule (age bands, co-ed minimums, pass-rush counts in flag).
One PLAYS_FOR edge per spell at a team: position and secondary_positions from the Positions chunk, jersey_number, role (starter, bench, practice_squad, injured_reserve, reserve, captain), depth_order, roster_list, arrangement (contract for pros, scholarship for college, amateur for rec and school; substitute for a one-off ringer, ended the same day), availability, availability_until, acquired_via, fee as text, contract_until.
role and roster_list are two different facts. role is what the player is to the team right now (starter, bench, captain, practice_squad, injured_reserve, reserve); roster_list is which of the league's lists they count against, in this pack's vocabulary: active (the 53), practice_squad, injured_reserve, pup (physically unable to perform), nfi (non-football injury), suspended, exempt. Write roster_list whenever a league counts lists (the pro and college levels); rec and school leagues leave it empty. Write role always. The two agree by construction: roster_list practice_squad goes with role practice_squad, roster_list injured_reserve with role injured_reserve, and every other non-active list with role reserve. Both live on the club edge only; a fantasy team's IR is slot IR on the separate fantasy_roster edge (Fantasy chunk) and never touches the club edge.
Reserve lists are roster designations, not health facts. Any player placed on a list that removes them from the active roster gets roster_list set to that list, role injured_reserve (or reserve for non-injury lists) and availability unavailable, with the placement, activation or return logged as a roster_move event (INVOLVED_IN the player role subject with detail naming the move, the team role to_team). A designated-to-return date is a lore chunk on the person titled "Roster designation" holding only the list's name and the dates ("injured_reserve, 2026-10-14; designated to return 2026-11-18"). Weekly injury-report statuses map to availability only: Out = unavailable, Doubtful = doubtful, Questionable = doubtful, no designation = available. The body part, the injury and any medical word never get stored, at any level.
Captains: role captain on PLAYS_FOR for season captains; PLAYED_IN captain true for game captains. Jersey numbers: 0-99; a change updates jersey_number in place with a lore note.
Coaching staff on STAFF_OF: head_coach; coordinator with unit offense/defense/special_teams and title "Offensive Coordinator", "Defensive Coordinator", "Special Teams Coordinator"; assistant_coach with title for position coaches ("Quarterbacks Coach", "Offensive Line Coach"); general_manager, owner, president, director with title. An interim head coach is head_coach with title "Interim Head Coach". A rec team's organiser is captain_organiser (with a PLAYS_FOR edge too if they play).

lore.title: Officials
lore.content: OFFICIATED role values: referee, umpire, down_judge, line_judge, field_judge, side_judge, back_judge (the full seven-person pro and college crew), replay_official, replay_assistant (pro and college replay booth), scorer (rec leagues that keep a book). School and rec crews are three to five officials; use referee for the white hat and the crew positions as named. The referee is the crew chief and the name fans know; record only the referee unless the owner names more. A disputed call is lore on the game titled "Key moments" or "Officiating", in the owner's words.

lore.title: Extended keys
lore.content: (none yet; keys the owner adds go here, one per line, dated)

lore.title: Recreational
lore.content:
What a local or amateur league changes. Flag football: 5v5 or 7v7, no tackling, 20-25 minute halves on a running clock, a 7-second pass clock, no-run zones, touchdowns 6 with 1- or 2-point conversions from the 5 or 10, interceptions returned score 6 (some leagues add 2 for a conversion-return); the sack key means a flag pull behind the line; rushing stats are rare or absent. A flag score is built only from 6 (touchdown), 1 or 2 (conversion, after a touchdown) and 2 (safety), so a total of 1, 3 or 5 cannot happen: treat it as a typo and ask before saving. Rec tackle and adult leagues: shorter quarters, running clock in the second half when the margin passes a mercy line (commonly 35 after halftime), decided_by run_rule when the game is called early. Co-ed leagues may require a woman to be an eligible receiver on a set number of plays; record the requirement in House rules, never per-play compliance.
Rolling subs and ringers: a one-off ringer is PLAYS_FOR with arrangement substitute and ended the same day (see rule/recording_a_match). Stat keeping is sporadic: most rec owners log the score and who scored. A touchdown by a named player with nothing else known is receiving_touchdowns (or rushing_touchdowns) 1 on a match line with every other key null; do not pad the line.
Overtime at this level is usually a college-style alternating possession from the 10 or 25, or none at all (ties stand). Record decided_by overtime either way and the format in House rules.
Youth and school leagues: everyone under 18 is is_minor true, first name and last initial, and the base rule/people_and_privacy applies in full. Weight-class and age-band eligibility is a House rules note on the competition, never a property on the child.
Rec standings: usually win_pct, head-to-head, points allowed, coin toss; some leagues award 2-1-0 league points (scoring_system 2-1-0) and then the table shows Pts instead of PCT.

lore.title: Professional
lore.content:
What the national 32-team professional league adds (college and other pro leagues differ; put their variations in a House rules chunk on the competition).
Overtime: regular season, one 10-minute period in which both teams get a possession unless the first ends in a safety or the second team fails to match; still level = tie. Playoffs: 15-minute periods, both teams possess, play until someone leads; no ties.
Calendar structure: 17 games over 18 weeks with one bye (Weeks 5-14), three preseason games, 14-team playoffs (seven per conference, seeds 1-7, the 1 seed rests in wildcard week), championship game at a neutral site that the league numbers (round "Championship Game <number>"), designated home team alternating by conference. Preseason and all_star never count.
Roster: 90 in camp, 53 after the late-August cutdown. Game day: 48 actives when at least eight are offensive linemen, otherwise 47; inactives are PLAYED_IN played false when tracked. Practice squad up to 16 (17 with an overseas-player exemption): role practice_squad, roster_list practice_squad, arrangement contract. Standard elevation up to three times a season per player without signing: a roster_move event dated the game day plus PLAYED_IN for the game, role and roster_list unchanged; signing to the 53 is a signing event, roster_list becomes active and role bench or starter.
Reserve lists (each placement and activation is a roster_move event): the injured list is roster_list injured_reserve, role injured_reserve, availability unavailable; designated-to-return players stay there until activated (eight returns per club per season). Physically-unable and non-football-injury lists: roster_list pup or nfi, role reserve, availability unavailable. Suspended list: roster_list suspended, role reserve, availability suspended, availability_until the date it lapses, the league's stated length and policy name in lore ("six games, performance-enhancing substances policy"), nothing else. Commissioner's exempt list: roster_list exempt, role reserve, availability unavailable. Activation sets roster_list active and role bench or starter. Nothing but the list name and dates is ever written about any of them.
Contracts and cap: fee is text on PLAYS_FOR ("4y/$160M, $100M gtd") and in INVOLVED_IN detail on the signing event. Extensions: signing event with detail starting "extension:", existing edge stays open, fee updated. Franchise and transition tags: signing event, detail "franchise tag, $X". Restructures and cap numbers: lore on the person titled "Contract", owner's wording. This world never computes cap space.
Free agency: new league year mid-March; signing with acquired_via free_agent; release ends the edge and sets person status free_agent; a successful waiver claim is a roster_move with acquired_via waiver on the new edge and the former club as from_team on the event; a claim that lost to a higher-priority club is recorded, when the owner wants it, as the same roster_move with status rejected and the winning club in detail.
Trades: one trade event, INVOLVED_IN each team role other with detail "sends: ... / receives: ...", each player traded_away or acquired with the destination club in detail. Draft picks are text in detail ("2027 R2 (own)", "2027 R4 (via Team 13)", conditional picks spelled out), never entities. Trade deadline: 4:00 pm ET on the Tuesday after Week 9; a trade logged after it is a question, not a refusal.
Draft: one event per draft, event_type draft, named "<Competition> Draft <year>", date of day one, end_date day three, seven rounds. INVOLVED_IN person role drafted with detail "Round 1, Pick 32 (32 overall)" ("(comp)" for compensatory picks), team role drafting_team; PLAYS_FOR opens acquired_via draft, started the draft date, rookie terms in fee. Undrafted free agents: signing, acquired_via free_agent, detail "UDFA". A full draft is about 257 persons: confirm first and create in batches.
Honours: WON to the season with title in full: "Champion" (detail game number and score), "Most Valuable Player", "Offensive Player of the Year", "Defensive Player of the Year", "Offensive Rookie of the Year", "Defensive Rookie of the Year", "Comeback Player of the Year", "Coach of the Year", "First-team All-League", "All-Star"; "Championship Game MVP" is WON to the final event.
Modern stats the owner may bring from public sources (expected points added, success rate, pressure rate, air yards, separation) are not in the key list; add them under Extended keys when asked, with the source named, since definitions differ by site.

lore.title: Fantasy
lore.content:
Fantasy leagues in this sport are run by rule/app_fantasy (the shared fantasy app: rosters, lineups, waivers, trades, drafts, matchups, standings). A fantasy competition carries sport american_football and level fantasy, and both that app and this pack APPLY_TO it. This chunk supplies only what is specific to American football.

One person per real player. The club edge is PLAYS_FOR with arrangement contract; each fantasy roster edge is a second PLAYS_FOR with arrangement fantasy_roster and slot. Never create a second person for the fantasy side; search by name and external_id first. Real production is a match-scope stat_line RECORDED_IN the real game (tagged american_football and the real season tag). Fantasy production is a separate match-scope stat_line RECORDED_IN the fantasy matchup event (tagged fantasy, american_football and the fantasy season tag) holding fantasy_points and projected_points and, if the manager wants, the real keys below repeated with source import. The two may disagree (stat corrections, platform quirks): the real line is what happened, the fantasy line is what scored. Bye events on the real side (event_type bye) are what the app reads to warn about a starter on bye.

Lineup slots (PLAYS_FOR.slot and PLAYED_IN.slot). Each slot takes the positions listed; BN, IR and TAXI never score.
QB    quarterback: QB
RB    running back: RB, FB
WR    wide receiver: WR
TE    tight end: TE
FLEX  RB, WR or TE
SFLX  superflex: QB, RB, WR or TE
RWR   RB or WR flex (some platforms)
WRT   same as FLEX, when the platform names it so; prefer FLEX
K     placekicker: K
DST   team defence and special teams: the real team entity, position DST
DL    IDP defensive line: DE, DT, NT, EDGE
LB    IDP linebacker: OLB, ILB, MLB, LB, EDGE when the league classes edge rushers as LB
DB    IDP defensive back: CB, NB, FS, SS, S, DB
IDP   IDP flex: any defensive position
BN    bench
IR    injured reserve slot (a lineup slot; no reason is ever recorded)
TAXI  dynasty taxi squad (role taxi on the edge as well)
Write the slot code only; RB1 and RB2 are both slot RB. Default lineup, when House rules is silent: QB 1, RB 2, WR 2, TE 1, FLEX 1, K 1, DST 1, BN 6, IR 1 (roster 15). Superflex leagues add SFLX 1. IDP leagues add DL 2, LB 2, DB 2 and usually drop K or DST.

Scoring formats (competition.scoring_system): standard, half_ppr, ppr, te_premium (ppr plus 0.5 per TE reception), superflex (a lineup setting, but platforms label leagues by it; combine as ppr-superflex in House rules), idp (any of the above plus defensive scoring), custom.

Default scoring table (half_ppr; House rules lists only the lines that differ). fantasy_points on a player line should equal this table applied to the real keys when both are present; the platform's figure wins and a mismatch is noted, per rule/app_fantasy.
Passing:   passing_yards 0.04 per yard (1 per 25); passing_touchdowns 4; interceptions_thrown -2; two_point_conversions 2 (passer, rusher and receiver all score it); passing_yards 300+ bonus 0 (3 when House rules says); 
Rushing:   rushing_yards 0.1 per yard (1 per 10); rushing_touchdowns 6; rushing_yards 100+ bonus 0 (3 when House rules says)
Receiving: receptions 0.5 (standard 0, ppr 1, te_premium 1.5 for TE); receiving_yards 0.1; receiving_touchdowns 6; receiving_yards 100+ bonus 0
Ball security: fumbles_lost -2
Returns:   kick_return_touchdowns 6; punt_return_touchdowns 6 (return yards usually 0; House rules when not)
Kicking:   extra_points_made 1; fg_made_under_40 3; fg_made_40_49 4; fg_made_50_plus 5; field goals missed -1 (DERIVED = field_goals_attempted - field_goals_made; platforms vary, House rules)
Team unit (DST), from the real team's match line and the opponent's score: defensive_sacks 1; takeaways: interceptions 2 and fumble_recoveries 2 (use the defence's interceptions and fumble_recoveries, i.e. the opponent's interceptions_thrown and fumbles_lost); defensive and return touchdowns 6; safeties 2; blocked_kicks 2; points allowed, from the opponent's final score: 0 → 10, 1-6 → 7, 7-13 → 4, 14-20 → 1, 21-27 → 0, 28-34 → -1, 35+ → -4 (platforms differ on whether return touchdowns against count; House rules). Store dst_points_allowed on the unit's fantasy line when the platform's definition differs from the final score.
IDP (when scoring_system idp): tackles_solo 1; tackles_assisted 0.5; sacks 2; interceptions 3; forced_fumbles 2; fumble_recoveries 2; passes_defended 1; interception_touchdowns and fumble_touchdowns 6; safeties 2; blocked_kicks 2.

Fantasy keys on player (or team-unit) match lines, in addition to the universal fantasy_points and projected_points:
fantasy_points_standard, fantasy_points_ppr   the same week under other formats, when the owner wants cross-league comparison (optional; stored from the platform)
dst_points_allowed       points the unit was charged with, when it differs from the opponent's final score
snap_share               DERIVED = snaps_offense / team total_plays, when both are tracked; otherwise store as given by the platform with source import
target_share             DERIVED = targets / team pass_attempts
Fantasy keys on the fantasy team's round-scope line (RECORDED_IN the matchup): optimal_points, bench_points, projected_total, as rule/app_fantasy defines them.
Season aggregates: fantasy_points on a season-scope player line RECORDED_IN the fantasy season, with games_played; points_per_game DERIVED = fantasy_points / games_played.

Calendar conventions: round is the real "Week N" so the two seasons line up; a fantasy regular season is Weeks 1-14 (14 teams or 17-week leagues: 1-15), playoffs the next two or three weeks, never the real season's final week unless House rules says so. The trade deadline is a House rules line, commonly the real Week 10-12. Draft: late in the real preseason, after the final cutdown; keeper declarations before it. Rookie drafts in dynasty leagues follow the real draft in spring.

Real keys this chunk reads (spelled as this pack's Stat keys spell them; the fantasy side yields to this pack if they ever differ): passing_yards, passing_touchdowns, interceptions_thrown, two_point_conversions, rushing_yards, rushing_touchdowns, receptions, receiving_yards, receiving_touchdowns, fumbles_lost, kick_return_touchdowns, punt_return_touchdowns, extra_points_made, field_goals_made, field_goals_attempted, fg_made_under_40, fg_made_40_49, fg_made_50_plus, tackles_solo, tackles_assisted, sacks, interceptions, forced_fumbles, fumble_recoveries, passes_defended, interception_touchdowns, fumble_touchdowns, safeties, blocked_kicks, defensive_sacks, takeaways, snaps_offense, targets, total_plays, pass_attempts.

lore.title: Glossary
lore.content: Bye: the one week a team does not play. Wild card: a playoff team that did not win its division. Seed: playoff ranking per conference or bracket. Sweep: beating a division rival twice in a season. Pick six: interception returned for a touchdown (interception_touchdowns). Scoop and score: fumble returned for a touchdown. Two-minute warning: automatic stoppage at 2:00 of each half (pro only). Touchback: kick in the end zone, ball to the 20 (punt) or 35 (pro kickoff, current rules). Safety: 2 points. Designated to return: an injured-list player cleared by the club to practise and return. Cutdown day: the 53-man deadline. Practice squad elevation: game-day call-up without a 53-man signing. Franchise tag: one-year tender keeping a free agent. Cap: the salary cap, text only in this world. UDFA: undrafted free agent. Mercy rule: running clock or early finish past a margin, rec and school (decided_by run_rule). No-run zone: flag-league area where the offense must pass. White hat: the referee.

lore.title: Season calendar
lore.content:
Typical year for the national pro league (dates shift a few days each year; the owner's season lore wins):
- February: championship game (first or second Sunday). Season stage then becomes offseason.
- Late February/early March: scouting combine. Early March: franchise tag deadline.
- Mid-March: new league year and free agency open (negotiating window two days before). Trades allowed from the new league year.
- Late April: draft, Thursday to Saturday, seven rounds.
- May: schedule release, rookie minicamp, organised team activities. June: mandatory minicamp.
- Late July: training camp. August: three preseason weekends, roster cut to 53 the Tuesday after the last preseason game, practice squads set the next day.
- Thursday after Labor Day: Week 1 (kickoff game hosted by the champion). 18 weeks, byes Weeks 5-14, Thanksgiving games in Week 12 or 13, Christmas games when the calendar allows, Week 18 all-divisional.
- Tuesday after Week 9, 4 pm ET: trade deadline.
- Mid-January: wildcard weekend, divisional, conference championships, a bye week, then the championship game.
College: late August to early December regular season, conference championships the first December weekend, bowls and the playoff through early January. School: August/September to November, state playoffs into December. Rec and flag: fall and spring sessions of 8-10 weeks plus a playoff weekend.
Store the current season's actual dates on the season (start_date = first game, end_date = final) and anything the owner cares about (their team's bye week, primetime games, a game abroad) in a lore chunk on the season titled "Calendar".

lore.title: Forfeits and abandonments
lore.content:
Forfeit: status forfeited, the league's awarded score in home_score/away_score (the pro league and most others record a forfeit as 2-0 to the non-offending team; some rec leagues use 1-0 or 6-0; follow House rules), score_display "2-0 (forfeit)", result accordingly, COMPETED_IN results win/loss, the reason in lore on the game unless it is medical (then no reason at all). A forfeit counts in the standings as a game played.
Abandoned (lightning, field conditions, light): status abandoned. If the league counts the score at stoppage as final (most do once the third quarter has started, or at a House-rules point), record the score, result and decided_by called_game with score_display "24-17 (called, 8:12 Q4, weather)". Otherwise result no_result and the position at stoppage in score_display; a replay ordered from scratch is a new event dated when it is played with round "Replay", and lore on both events pointing at each other. A game halted and finished on a later date from the point of stoppage is one event with status suspended until it resumes, date_* of day one and end_date the day it finished.
Postponed: status postponed, keep the entity, new date when known, original date in lore. Mercy rule: the game is complete; status completed, decided_by run_rule, the stopping point in score_display.
Double forfeit or no-contest: status cancelled, result no_result, lore note.

properties.trigger: a fan or player logging their team's week in American football: the weekend's result, the box score, inactives and elevations, the injury report, the bye, next week's kickoff, the playoff picture

data.short_description: The weekly routine for an owner who follows or plays on one American football team: result, box score, story, roster news, standings refresh, next game. Also how to load a whole schedule and record the bye.

lore.title: The weekly cycle
lore.content:
Owners who follow or play on a team bring the same things every week, whether the team is a pro franchise or a Thursday flag side. Handle them in this order, logging what you can before asking anything:
1. Result. Search for the game (season tag + round "Week N" + the two teams); it is usually already scheduled. Set status completed, scores, score_display when overtime, result, decided_by, and both COMPETED_IN results. Quarter scores go on each team's match stat_line (points_q1..points_ot), not on the event.
2. Box score, if the owner gives one. Team lines first (two stat_lines, scope match), then player lines for whoever they name. Use only pack keys; a number without a key is a question, asked once, with the offer to add it under Extended keys.
3. Story. Lore on the game: Summary, Key moments, Officiating, Conditions, in the owner's words.
4. Roster. Inactives (PLAYED_IN played false), elevations and reserve-list moves as roster_move events that update roster_list and role (injured list: roster_list injured_reserve, role injured_reserve; other lists: role reserve), injury-report statuses as availability only, any signing/release/trade as events. For a fantasy league in the same world, nothing here changes: the fantasy edge on the same person is rule/app_fantasy's business and reads this edge's availability and the team's bye event.
5. Standings. Update the owner's team's season line (wins/losses/ties, points_for/against, division_*, conference_*, home_*/away_*), as_of the game date, source derived, "Derived from" lore listing the games. Update the season's current_round to the week just logged, and stage when the playoffs start.
6. Next up. Find or create next week's game as status scheduled with the kickoff time and venue, or the bye event if it is the bye week. Mention it when you close.

lore.title: What the owner's team means
lore.content: The team tagged mine is the owner's team; there is at most one per sport in the world unless the owner says otherwise. Default every question to it ("how did we do", "who's our QB1", "are we in the playoff picture"). A partial table (only the owner's games logged) is normal: give their record, division record, conference record and streak from their own COMPETED_IN edges, and say which rivals' results you do not have rather than inventing them. Offer a web lookup for the rest only if the owner wants it and the competition is a public pro or college league, in which case opponents' results may be looked up and stored as events with source_url. Never look up a rec, school or youth league.

lore.title: Scheduling a whole season
lore.content: When the schedule drops (May for the pro league, a week before the session for a rec league), the owner may want every game plus the bye loaded. For the pro shape that is 18 events: show the list (week, opponent, home/away, date, time, network if given) and create on a yes in one batch, status scheduled, tagged with the season tag, each with COMPETED_IN edges and HELD_AT when the venue exists. Flex scheduling later changes date_* and date_hour; keep the entity, note the original slot in lore.
